<!-- pr-reviewer: 9673a77efe79e3ef73174599ac5299341e329f2a -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The design and the posted words look right, and every suite is green. The blocker is test coverage: under the standing rule, each new refusal and stamp field needs a test that fails when its line is deleted, and most of this PR's new refusal lines, plus its stamp field, survive deletion.

### What looks good
- The dialect is machine data with no defaults (`edm.taper_angle { positive, corner }`). A garbled word refuses the file, and an unstated one is refused by name at generation, never guessed. This is the shape #1164 asked for.
- The sign convention checks out. In `posting_wire::angled`, `cross = dx*t.y - dy*t.x` is the top's lean projected on the left normal of travel, so on the counter-clockwise punch the top leans inward (left) and `top_left` writes `A3`. The test pins the flip to `A-3` under `top_right`. The word's magnitude is `|taper_deg|` and its sign comes from the path, so a negative (narrowing) taper is handled by the same code.
- Frames are consistent. `top` (`hs.top`) and the CL `m.z` are both world, the post subtracts the origin through `wo()`, and `WirePlane` is `top - origin[2]`, which matches how `guide_planes` already adds `origin_z`.
- Under `mitre`, the CL equals #536's `wire_taper_punch.cl` byte for byte. Under `cone`, the lean is held at exactly 3 degrees through every corner (four quarter turns of 45 two-degree steps). The control's in-place turns are dropped from the NC, so the NC is the mitre's apart from the note line.
- Most importantly, the verify judges the path the stated rule cuts. `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post` shows the cone's rounded lower corner blocking the post (`wire gouge`) on a drafted punch that the mitre rule cuts clean.
- Interplay is sound. The U/V goldens (`wire_taper`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour`, `wire_verify`) pass unedited. A 4-axis cut (#537/#1181) on an angle-word machine is refused by name at generation. The no-`uv` refusal now names both dialects. Tabs and burnout with a taper keep their existing refusals.
- No `PROCESS_VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot PNG, `build.rs`, `.github`, script or dependency changes. Both new files carry a provenance line, and every touched file is under ~400 lines.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream main d0b117db, clean merge)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run` | ok |
| post lib + the 19 suites in the quick plan (incl. `script_wire_iso` 11, `script_sinker_iso` 22, `fanuc_post` 12) | all ok (47 lib tests + 136 suite tests) |
| motion `--lib` | 293 passed, 5 ignored |
| app: `wire_taper_angle` 4, `wire_taper` 6, `wire_4axis` 8, `wire_post` 8, `wire_contour` 8, `wire_stamp` 7, `wire_verify` 3, `wire_readers` 7, `wire_tabs` 4, `wire_burnout` 3 | all pass |
| app: `golden_cl` 32, `conformance` 7, `machine` 33, `edm_machine` 5, `edm_conditions` 2, `posting` 17, `recorded_post_streams` 5, `project_roundtrip` 73, `mcp_wire_contour` 4, `feature_pick_wire` 4 | all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Mutation check.** I deleted (or neutralised) each new refusal or stamp line and re-ran `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_stamp`, `wire_taper`, `wire_post`, `wire_4axis`, `script_wire_iso`, and the post and motion lib tests:

| Line | Result |
|---|---|
| `motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs` cone lead-in-at-corner refusal | killed |
| `edm_taper.rs` `complete()` (both arms); corner garble; `wire_op::corner_rule` 4-axis refusal; the cps `(nor an angle-word taper ...)` text | asserted by message in tests |
| `operation/wire_op.rs:176-177` stamp of `taper_angle` | **survived** |
| `wire-iso.cps:205` `angle4` | **survived** |
| `wire-iso.cps:210` `acode` | **survived** |
| `wire-iso.cps:216` `angtpl` | **survived** |
| `wire-iso.cps:305` `ang` | **survived** |
| `posting_wire.rs:166` 4-axis refusal | **survived** |
| `posting_wire.rs:170` `complete()` | **survived** |
| `posting_wire.rs:171` top unresolved | **survived** |
| `posting_wire.rs:326` lean changes side | **survived** |
| `posting_wire.rs:333` no leaning side | **survived** |
| `edm_taper.rs:89` not an object | **survived** |
| `edm_taper.rs:103` `positive` garble | **survived** |
| `edm.rs:81` `"taper_angle"` in `WIRE_KEYS` | **survived** |
| `taper.rs:222` cone turn-back | **survived** |

### Requested before merge
1. **Pin the stamp** (`crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs:176-177`). This one is safety-relevant. Without these lines, changing a machine's `corner` from `mitre` to `cone` (or from U/V to angle word) leaves the cached path fresh. A mitre path, judged by the verify as a mitre, would then post to a control that cuts cones. Please add a `wire_stamp` (or `wire_taper_angle`) test asserting that the stamp differs between the mitre and cone machines, and between the U/V and angle-word machines.
2. **Pin the cps refusals** (`assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:205, 210, 216, 305`) in `crates/post/tests/script_wire_iso.rs`, using hand-built streams:
   - `WireTaperDialect "angle"` with a zero taper or with `WireFourAxis`;
   - a machine missing `edm.codes.taper_angle`;
   - a `taper_angle` template without `{angle}`;
   - a `WireAngle` in a section with no dialect.

   The app refuses most of these first, so the script is the only guard for any other stream source.
3. **Pin the post-side refusals in `posting_wire.rs`** (`:166, :170, :171, :326, :333`). A unit test of `angled()` on hand-built records covers `:326` (a lean that changes side) and `:333` (no leaning side). Lines `:166` and `:170` duplicate the generation door. Either pin them (for example, generate on a complete machine, then post after the machine's rule is emptied) or drop them with a comment naming the door that makes them unreachable.
4. **Pin the parse and key refusals:**
   - `edm_taper.rs:89`: `taper_angle` that is not an object;
   - `edm_taper.rs:103`: a garbled `positive` word (only the `corner` garble is tested now);
   - `edm.rs:81`: a sinker machine stating `edm.taper_angle` is refused as a wire-only key. The existing loop over `WIRE_KEYS` in `edm_tests.rs:135` cannot catch the key being dropped from the list, so this needs a test that names `taper_angle`.
5. **Pin the cone turn-back refusal** (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs:222`) with a motion unit test on a ring that reverses on itself.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The commit `39d014d8` uses `style(edm):`. `style` is not one of the types AGENTS.md lists; `refactor` or `chore` would fit. It is harmless in a merge-commit history.
- Under `cone`, safety at concave (die) corners rests on the verify. The arc about the top corner overshoots the lower-plane offset there, as it rounds the convex one. A die fixture under `cone` in `wire_taper_angle` would show that the verify catches the re-entrant case too, not only the punch.
- `positive` is stamped though it does not shape the path. That is harmless: it only forces a regeneration.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b1c287a0ae467b40edc1357ac9658703aec35dd3 -->
**This head passes the review. The branch conflicts with `main`.** The new commit resolves all five requests from the review of `9673a77e`. No code blocker remains.

### What the new commit changes
The delta is one commit, `b1c287a0`. It adds tests. It also moves one block of code into a new function, `angle_lean()` in `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs`. I compared that function with the old code. The messages and the results are the same. The commit changes no golden and no snapshot.

### The five requests: all resolved
1. **The stamp.** `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` now has `the_corner_rule_and_the_dialect_each_move_the_stamp`. It tests three pairs. The mitre rule differs from the cone rule. The U/V machine differs from each angle-word machine. When a rule in the machine file changes, the cached path becomes stale. This closes the safety-relevant item.
2. **The script refusals.** `crates/post/tests/script_wire_iso.rs` now has `an_angle_word_section_posts_and_each_missing_piece_is_refused_by_name`. It builds its own streams. It checks each refusal line in `wire-iso.cps`: zero taper, a 4-axis cut, a missing code, a bad template, and an angle word with no dialect.
3. **The post-side refusals.** `crates/app/src/posting_wire_tests.rs` now has two tests. They cover `angle_lean()` and `angled()`. I accept your choice to keep lines 166/170/171 as the post's own guard, and to test them through the new function. The guard now covers a path that reaches the post another way.
4. **The parse and key refusals.** `crates/post/src/machine/edm_taper.rs` tests a value that is not an object, and a wrong side word. `crates/post/src/machine/edm_tests.rs` now names `taper_angle` in a test of its own. A dropped key cannot pass silently.
5. **The cone turn-back refusal.** `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs` now has `the_cone_rule_refuses_a_ring_that_turns_back_on_itself`. I checked the test ring myself. The turn is 180 degrees at the third point, and the lead-in check passes before it. The second part checks a normal ring.

Each test names a refusal message that is in the source. I read both sides. I did not repeat the mutation runs; your table in the PR body states them.

### Local results (the PR head alone, not merged with main)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib` | ok: 49 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_wire_iso` | ok: 12 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` | ok: 292 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | ok: 186 passed |
| app suites: `posting` 17, `wire_post` 8, `wire_taper` 6, `wire_4axis` 8, `wire_stamp` 7, `wire_contour` 8, `wire_verify` 3, `wire_taper_angle` 5 | all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I built in a local worktree, not on the runner. The runner merges with `main` first, and that merge fails now (see below). The runner was otherwise free: two `camcraft-pr-test` runners online, no cut running.

### Safety note for this EDM work
This PR changes posted output for a machine that states the angle-word dialect. A wrong "ok" would let a bad machine-file reading, or a bad corner path, reach a real cut. The guards are in place now: every refusal has its test, and the verify blocks a cone path that gouges. These tests do not exercise a real EDM control (D10). They also model the lead-in and lead-out ramp as linear, as in #536. The PR body states both.

### Requested before merge
1. **The conflict with `main`.** The files `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs` and `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs` conflict. This is merge-time work, not a code finding. When the merge batch reaches this PR, merge `origin/main` into the branch, re-run the quick gate, and push. The review then stands for that refresh.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The `style(edm):` subject in `39d014d8` stays in the branch history. As said before, it is harmless.
- The die-corner idea from the review of `9673a77e` stays open as a later test, not a blocker here.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
